sourcePolicy: Use public lexical sources as corroborating evidence, not as self-approving production data.
Preserve the pinned STEPBible/TBESG/TFLSJ source lock from the Luke v4 track as the canonical source family; public web-accessible aggregations are intake corroboration only.
Do not flatten classical/full-lexicon extensions into Luke-specific meanings without exact Luke context support.
Morphology and token counts constrain usage but are not independent lexical senses.
This pass does not close the exact Luke morphology gate; exact token/morphology extraction remains required.

sources.note: Public TBESG/LSJ/Dodson aggregation gives hagios as holy/sacred/set apart and lists Luke uses beginning at Luke 1:15; person, thing and divine-reference uses must remain context-distinguished.
Public TBESG/LSJ/Dodson aggregation gives agkale as the bent arm/arm and explicitly identifies Luke 2:28 as its sole NT occurrence.
Public TBESG/LSJ/Dodson aggregation gives agnoeo as not know/be ignorant/not understand and explicitly cites Luke 9:45 under the not-understand sense.
Public TBESG/LSJ/Dodson aggregation gives agora as assembly/place of assembly/marketplace and explicitly cites Luke 7:32, 11:43 and 20:46 for the public-marketplace sense.

Public TBESG/LSJ/Dodson aggregation gives agorazo as buy/purchase, while broader metaphorical redeem senses occur elsewhere; Luke occurrences include ordinary purchase contexts such as Luke 9:13, 14:18-19, 17:28, 19:45 and 22:36.
Public TBESG/LSJ/Dodson aggregation distinguishes the act of catching from the concrete catch/haul and explicitly cites Luke 5:4 and 5:9.
Public LSJ/Dodson/TBESG aggregation gives agrauleo as live/stay outdoors or in the field, with Luke 2:8 as the sole NT occurrence.
Public TBESG/LSJ/Dodson aggregation distinguishes field, country/country places/farms, and a piece of land; Luke 8:34 and 9:12 are explicitly cited under country places/farms.

targets.lexicalIntake: Public lexical evidence supports holy/sacred/set apart. Luke-specific contexts must distinguish Holy Spirit/divine reference, holy persons, and holy things instead of collapsing all tokens into one theological definition.
The public lexical evidence is narrow and concrete: bent arm/arm, with Luke 2:28 the sole NT occurrence. No figurative sense is imported without evidence.

Public lexical evidence distinguishes not know/be ignorant from not understand; Luke 9:45 is explicitly tied to the latter. Willful ignorance is not promoted into the lexical head without contextual evidence.

Public lexical evidence preserves assembly/place-of-assembly history but Luke citations support the public square/marketplace sense. The candidate must not flatten every occurrence to commercial 'market' if the social/public-square function is primary.

Public lexical evidence gives buy/purchase as the ordinary sense. Metaphorical redeem/purchase senses found elsewhere in the NT must not be injected into Luke tokens unless the exact Luke context supports them.
Public TBESG evidence explicitly distinguishes the action of catching at Luke 5:4 from the concrete catch/haul at Luke 5:9; both senses must remain separate in Korean.
Public lexical evidence is narrow: live/stay outdoors, especially in the field, even at night. Luke 2:8 should govern the Korean candidate rather than derivational speculation.

Public lexical evidence distinguishes field, country/country places/farms, and a piece of land. Exact Luke contexts must decide among cultivated field, rural country/farms, and owned land rather than forcing a single gloss.
